title: How To Be A Confident Teacher Amid The Raging Storm
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Writing during a period he describes as marked by rising disrespect and teacher burnout, Linsin argues that confidence is something teachers must build themselves rather than wait for outside conditions to improve. His central prescription is to double-down on classroom management: sharply defined boundaries and consistent accountability, rather than experimenting with disparate strategies, are what create the 'undeniable aura' of a teacher students respect. He insists that students can sense fear and timidity, so a teacher's inner uncertainty leaks outward and invites misbehavior. Beyond classroom systems, he urges teachers to take ownership of their own mindset and to manage their personal lives well — sleep, exercise, time away from work — because being mentally depleted undermines the vigilance and steadiness teaching requires. He closes with a defiant, almost manifesto-like insistence that a peaceful, well-behaved class is still possible for any teacher who takes responsibility.
points: Confidence has to be built by the teacher through classroom management, not handed to them by circumstances improving.
Sharply defined boundaries and consistent accountability, not scattered new strategies, produce the 'aura' of a confident leader.
Students sense fear and timidity immediately, so unresolved inner uncertainty invites misbehavior.
Taking full personal responsibility, rather than blaming students or circumstances, is the first step toward real confidence.
Managing one's personal life — sleep, exercise, time away from school — directly supports the vigilance classroom management demands.
quotes: Confidence in particular is at an all-time low. I hear it from my colleagues and coaching clients. I see it in the comment section of this website.

This is critical because students can sense fear and timidity from a mile away, and they’re sensing a lot of it these days. You must be confident, especially in this climate, or they’ll roll right over you.
Instead, you must double-down on sharply defined boundaries and consistent accountability. You must be a pro who knows the why of what you’re doing and how it fits into a cohesive whole.
Again, they can sense when you’re feeling beat down and afraid. They know when you’re walking on eggshells and hoping they’ll behave. It’s something you can’t hide.
It’s possible, even now, to have the peaceful, well-behaved class you desire. You’re wrong if you think otherwise.
